rename.resolution: Re-verdicted rename -> declined; no ours-half, so the suffix question does not arise. Consistent with cpp:Client::take_type_erased_response and cpp:Subscription::take_type_erased. No code change; no target name invented.

why:
RE-VERDICTED 2026-08-26 (phase-379 W5), rename -> declined. Same evidence as `cpp:Client::take_type_erased_response`.
`ServiceBase::take_type_erased_request(void * request_out, rmw_request_id_t & request_id_out)` erases over a DESERIALIZED request STRUCT -- the function the typed `Service::take_request` forwards to (`service.hpp:452`). Ours is `Service<S>::take_request(RequestType& req, int64_t& seq_id)`, a template on the concrete type, and it already belongs to `cpp:Service::take_request`. The byte form underneath (`nros_cpp_service_server_take_request_raw`, `nros_cpp_ffi.h:1553`) is FFI, not a user-facing C++ method, and belongs to the SERIALIZED/RAW rows. Note ours carries a bare `int64_t seq_id` where rclcpp carries `rmw_request_id_t`; that difference is its own row (`rust:RequestId` / `rust:rmw_request_id_t`, verdict divergence).
Not a gap: a runtime type-erased take needs rosidl typesupport resolved at runtime and a heap-allocated message struct to take into -- exactly what `cpp:Subscription::create_message` declines for the no-allocator reason. Kept consistent with `cpp:Subscription::take_type_erased` (pubsub), decided the same day on the same evidence. (CORRECTED 2026-09-04, phase-417: the prose named `Service<S>::try_recv_request` and `nros_cpp_service_server_try_recv_raw` in the present tense; both were retired by phase-379 W6 decision 1.)
